newsitem.title: CHINA: China sees Hong Kongers as shrewd and cultivated.
newsitem.headline: China sees Hong Kongers as shrewd and cultivated.

text.p: Hong Kong Chinese have made a good impression on their new fellow countrymen with 82 percent of mainlanders giving them glowing reports, an official newspaper said on Wednesday.

A survey of mainland Chinese attitudes toward inhabitants of the former British colony that returned to Chinese rule on July 1 showed 82.0 percent of mainlanders had a good impression of Hong Kong people, the Procuratorial Daily said.

The survey of 1,000 urban Chinese adults revealed Hong Kongers were seen as "rich", "diligent", "good at business", "pragmatic", "cultivated", "relaxed" and "friendly", but the most common description was "shrewd", it said.
Residents of the southern city of Guangzhou were particularly impressed by the inhabitants of neighbouring Hong Kong, considering them above all to be "cultivated", it said.

The survey also showed Hong Kong was Guangzhou's second favourite international city after Paris, and China's fifth most popular tourist destination after the United States, Japan, Singapore and France, it said.
The survey contrasted with the opinions of many average Chinese, especially in northern cities, who regard Hong Kong residents as uneducated boors interested only in money.
